private_note: I weigh each fifth at one-in-five and care more about avoiding the bottom than about winning big. Alder has the same average as Today but a much better floor (32 vs 22) and guaranteed health coverage, so it beats Today outright. Cedar's higher average doesn't make up for a 15k floor with no coverage. Hazel and Birch give up 20-22 percent of the average for a better floor, and that costs me too much in four of five draws.
statement: Fellow delegates, each of us faces the same lottery: a one-in-five chance of every group. So I ask: which plan gives a household the best deal across all five draws? Alder keeps average income where it is today, 100, but raises the lowest fifth from 22 to 32 and guarantees health coverage to everyone. The cost falls lightly on the top fifth, 242 instead of 252. That is cheap insurance against the worst draw. Cedar raises the average, but a one-in-five chance of living on 15 thousand with no coverage is a gamble I won't take. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom, but they cut the average by a fifth, which leaves most of us worse off. We need nine votes, and if we fail we get Today. Alder is better than Today for nearly any draw that matters. I urge you to rally behind it.
